subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron overflow recovery silently retain only five quarantine archives, or must recovery records remain non-destructive until an explicit doctor-owned or user-visible cleanup contract exists?
rationale: The PR changes persistent recovery data from indefinite preservation to automatic deletion; correctness tests cannot determine whether that loss is an acceptable product and operational policy.

options.title: Use non-destructive recovery handling
options.body: Keep bounded reads and overflow recovery, but do not delete older quarantine archives until an explicit cleanup/recovery owner and user-facing contract exist.

options.title: Accept five-file retention
options.body: Explicitly approve silent deletion of the oldest recovery archive after the fifth retained archive as the permanent operational policy.

options.title: Pause archive rotation policy
options.body: Land neither archive pruning nor further retention behavior until the cron persistence owner defines the recovery-data lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Use non-destructive recovery handling
recommendation.body: Keep bounded reads and overflow recovery, but do not delete older quarantine archives until an explicit cleanup/recovery owner and user-facing contract exist.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely repository-level owner for a core persisted-state and recovery-policy choice; current code-history attribution could not be established more precisely from the available read-only inspection.
